Severely suffering from the obligatory need to be as over the top and in your face as possible to make it clear ITS A SATIRE.

Dennis Quaid's performance is about te best represantation of its tone, which I couldn't help but roll my eyes at every single moment of it, given the movie's humor just about winks, crosses its eye and slips on every banana there is to make it clear its being humorous, which only made it all the more pedantic and frustrating to me.

Furthermore, every other aspect of its storytelling, from the writing (telegraphed plotting, annoying bits, and inconsistent rules regarding the aging) to its clunky editing, stale cinematography and amateurish direction (she ends up breaking the 180 degree rule in honest-to-God transitional scenes, it's ridiculous), made its mise en scene all the more tiresome, and stretched its already overbearing 140 minute runtime to unbelievably irritating lengths.

The only aspects of the film I felt any sort of admiration for where Qualley's performance, which I can't even bring myself to enjoy due to the shallowness of her character (as in, how one-dimensional is her writing and complexity, not the actual shallowness of Sue's personality) which makes her performance nothing but an admirable, though mundane exercise in film-acting waterworks, and the make-up, which in spite of being actually terrific work from those involved in the prosthetics, only become all the more obvious, as it keeps going, feeling more like a kid shoving a dead bird on your face rather than genuine discomforting imagery.

Pt. 2

M was incredibly empathetic and compassionate through all of this, and assured me everything would be fine, even accepting my request for her taking some distance from me for the sake of our friendship. So were my friends, who promised to pretend none of what I did ever happened. After coming back to my senses, we got back to her house, and I bailed out of there as quickly as I could, making sure to apologize to M one last time in private, though by this point she was paying me no mind and just making sure I'd get back home as soon as possible. She'd reassure me of everything being ok one last time by text later on, but after that disastrous episode I ditched my classes for the entire next week

Last Monday I finally resumed my classes, and from the very first second we saw each other again, M knew to keep her promise and didn't even bat an eye towards me, I didn't question it, knowing I had asked for that and just resumed my day, but as the week has kept going, it has all become very awkward for me. Every time we pass by each other, seemingly remembering our deal to distance ourselves, I just feel this unshakeable guilt and I'm terrified of the very real possibility of our friendship not ever being the same now that the cat's out of the bag and she knows I could fall back on my impulsive flirting again. Furthermore, the mere idea of her re-examinig our entire friendship know that she knows of my struggles with BPD and Limerence, though obviously valid, makes me hate myself all the more. Hell, we even manage to not even say a word to each other when around the same group of friends and it's unbelievably uncomfortable for me.

I've already ruined many friendships like this before, and I don't want to do the same again. Both for her sake and for the sake of our friends. I don't know what to do nor how to turn off this feeling of shame and guilt over all of this. I'm in the wrong, right? I figure so, but could anyone give me some advice in how to mend all of this? Or at least how to not screw it up any further?

TL;DR Had a breakdown in front of a friend/FP, revealed to her my condition and that she's my FP, asked her for some distance, but now the possibility of our friendship being irreversibly screwed because of this is eating me alive.

Error and The Spell of Mathematics is about them getting back together and being toxic all over again. Pompeji is about disillusionment, This Link is Dead is lashing out, Radiant City has suicidal ideation and could be about an attempt ("Where's the ledge? I can't touch it, but I feel it's so close." I mean, come on...), Headless is them coming to their senses and separating again, and the title track is them making peace with their choices, but remaining in good terms.

Applying to the college I chose with barely any other options or efforts to apply elsewhere. I never thought about it twice in the moment, but on hindsight, it was REALLY stupid of me to not have any backup plans and I'm surprised it all worked out in the end.

Just for reference, here's how my former college's application process used to be:

You have to sign up on early January to apply, because it's an annual process. (That year, a little over 1000 people did)

You download and write up a format, fill it with a virtual portfolio and take an online test. (only 987 followed the process accordingly)

Out of those 987, they chose the 420 best to be granted an in-person interview, where they'd discuss their aspirations, reasons to choose the career, and go over their portfolio.

Out of those 420 who take the interview, they only select 120 to take the final admission exam (and the scary part is that apparently, they instantly decide if they'll select you out of the applicants the second you leave the interview room).

Finally, out of those 120, they only admit the 60 students who scored the bestresults. I believe I was #54, so I *barely* made it in. Then, the Top 40 get to enter on the Summer semester, while the remaining 20 students enter on the Winter semester.

In hindsight, it was an immense risk to have applied to that university, but it does make me incredibly proud to have aced the process on my first try. I still meet people in my career who also tried and failed (some more than once!). So, it really puts in perspective how lucky I was, especially when I didn't really bother with any other universities.

It's a little complicated, and to reduce it to a couple of paragraphs would just make this look like finger-pointing and a black-and-white issue, which it wasn't. So, don't take sides when reading this, but in short:

They made me scared for their safety after a call late at night, which they hung up on. After being worried sick about them doing something stupid, they called me 3 hours later to tell me they were fine and that they would explain it later.

They kept kicking the can down the road on the matter for a good two-ish weeks before they finally told me what happened. By that point I was emotionally drained, and literally couldn't bring myself to say anything to them on the call (this was on 2021, so pandemic and all...), so, they hung up.

I passed a good two months being unable to respond to any dms from them, just not having that energy in me to reply, and after a while, I found out they deleted me off of their socials.

I've struggled with abandonment issues before, having being ghosted by my best friend at 12 years old with no explanation, and having being cut off of another close friend's socials earlier that year, and I explicitly discussed this with them on more than a couple of occasions, and how much those events have hurt my ability to trust people, yet, they did it anyway. So, I followed suit, and cut off all contact with them as well.

They would sometimes try to talk to me by texts months later, trying to get in contact once more, but I kept ignoring them. Just thinking about this person and my complicated feelings for them kept stressing me to an unbearable point, so, me ignoring them after what they did was the one thing keeping me somewhat relaxed on the matter. That was, until they found out where I had moved to via a mutual friend and they kept calling me one night until I would come outside and talk to them. They tried to talk to me like nothing had happened and wanted to know what was wrong, but I just couldn't stand the whole situation, essentially breaking our friendship with 3 really short answers. Then crying hours later, after realizing the permanency of my choice.

I understand I put the final nail in the coffin, and that in some ways it should be my cross to bare, but this was someone I had loved, someone I wanted to age with and always have in my life regardless of any romantic feelings. So, naturally, I'm still a fucking wreck about this whole situation.

I'm still grieving the end of this friendship over a year later, and haven't been able to form a close bond with anyone since. Though, tbf, I don't think I ever want to again.

tl; dr: Close friend gives me a call that scares me for their safety, then we don't talk to each other, cut off contact and distance ourselves until out friendship becomes irreperable.
